sections.heading: CVE / CWE / NVD — Relationships
items: CVE = specific vulnerability instance in specific software (CVE-YEAR-NUMBER, maintained by MITRE/CISA)
CWE = weakness category — the class of vulnerability (CWE-89 = SQL Injection, maintained by MITRE)
NVD = enriched CVE database with CVSS scores, patch info, exploit availability (NIST, nvd.nist.gov)
CVE maps to CWE: CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) → CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data)

sections.heading: CVSS v3.1 Score Ranges
items: 0.0 = None
4.0–6.9 = Medium
9.0–10.0 = Critical
CVSS = technical severity only. Business risk = CVSS + exposure + exploitability in context + asset value

sections.heading: OWASP Top 10 (2021)
items: A01: Broken Access Control — users acting outside intended permissions
A02: Cryptographic Failures — weak/absent encryption at rest or in transit
A03: Injection — untrusted data interpreted as commands (SQL, OS, LDAP)
A04: Insecure Design — fundamental design flaws (no rate limiting, logic flaws)
A05: Security Misconfiguration — defaults, unnecessary features, verbose errors
A06: Vulnerable and Outdated Components — unpatched libraries, plugins, servers
A07: Identification and Authentication Failures — weak auth, session management
A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures — supply chain, unsigned updates, deserialisation
A09: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures — insufficient detection capability
A10: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — server fetches attacker-controlled URLs

sections.heading: NIST Cybersecurity Framework — Five Functions
items: Identify — Know your assets, risks, and current controls
Protect — Implement safeguards to limit security event impact
Detect — Identify security events through monitoring and logging
Respond — Contain, eradicate, and communicate after detection
Recover — Restore capabilities; improve from incident lessons

sections.heading: Tool Categories by VAPT Phase
items: Reconnaissance (Phase 2): Nmap, theHarvester, Shodan, Maltego, OSINT Framework
Scanning & Enumeration (Phase 3): Nessus, OpenVAS, Nikto, Gobuster/ffuf
Web Application Testing (Phases 3+4): Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, SQLMap
Exploitation (Phase 4): Metasploit, Cobalt Strike (red team), Havoc
Credential Testing (Phases 3+4): Hashcat, John the Ripper, Hydra, CrackMapExec
Traffic Analysis (All phases): Wireshark, tcpdump
Post-Exploitation (PTES Phase 6): Mimikatz, BloodHound, PowerView

sections.heading: Certification Pathway — Offensive Security
items: Entry: Security+ (knowledge, broadly recognised) | eJPT (practical, entry-level offensive)
Intermediate: CEH (knowledge, HR-recognised globally) | PNPT (fully practical, practitioner-respected)
Advanced: OSCP (24-hour practical exam, industry gold standard) | CPTS (10-day exam, highly rigorous)
Rule: build practical skill first (Hack The Box, TryHackMe, eJPT); pursue OSCP when HTB Medium machines take < 4 hours consistently
